column1: Implement Database UML Structure
column30:
*User Story*  
As a systems analyst, I’d like to design and document the system’s database structure using UML so that the development team has a clear, shared understanding of the data model, entity relationships, and integrity rules before implementation begins.

The UML database diagrams should identify the core entities, their attributes, primary and foreign keys, and the relationships between them. This structure will guide database implementation, support the functional requirements, and reduce data-modeling issues early in development.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* A UML class/entity-relationship diagram is created for the system database structure.
* The diagram includes all major entities required for the system, including entities related to users, service providers, administrators, and relevant system processes.
* Each entity includes its key attributes, including primary keys and applicable foreign keys.
* Relationships between entities are clearly shown, including cardinality (for example, one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-many).
* The design identifies any required junction tables for many-to-many relationships.
* Database constraints and business rules, such as required fields, unique values, and referential integrity requirements, are documented where applicable.
* All entities and relationships map back to the system’s functional requirements and use cases.
* The database structure is reviewed for completeness, consistency, and support for anticipated edge cases.

column1: Add Swagger/OpenAPI documentation and UI to Project
column30:
Currently, our project does not have an interactive API documentation interface. Integrating Swagger (Swashbuckle / OpenAPI) will allow developers, QA, and frontend consumers to explore endpoints, inspect request/response schemas, and execute test requests directly through an interactive UI.


h3. *Scope of Work:*

* Install necessary Swagger/OpenAPI NuGet packages ({{Swashbuckle.AspNetCore}}).
* Configure Swagger generation in service registration ({{Program.cs}} / {{Startup.cs}}).
* Configure Swagger UI middleware (typically enabled for Development and Staging environments).
* Enable XML documentation generation in the {{.csproj}} file to surface triple-slash ({{///}}) code comments in the UI.



h3. Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1: Swagger UI availability in allowed environments
  Given the API application is running in a local or Development/Staging environment
  When a user navigates to {{/swagger}} or {{/swagger/index.html}}
  Then the Swagger UI dashboard should render successfully without console errors.

Scenario 2: Endpoint discovery and schema accuracy
  Given the Swagger UI is open
  When viewing the list of controller endpoints
  Then all active API endpoints, HTTP methods, route parameters, and query parameters should be visible
  And request/response body schemas (models and status codes: 200, 400, 401, 404, 500) should match the codebase.

Scenario 3: XML documentation integration
  Given an endpoint or model with triple-slash ({{/// <summary>}}) XML comments in code
  When inspected in Swagger UI
  Then the summary descriptions and parameter explanations should be visible on the corresponding endpoints and models.

Scenario 4: Security definition (JWT Bearer Auth - Optional/If Applicable)
  Given the API uses token-based authentication
  When a user clicks the "Authorize" button in Swagger UI and provides a valid Bearer token
  Then subsequent "Try it out" API requests should include the {{Authorization: Bearer <token>}} header.

column1: Backend: Provider slot creation API
column30:
A slot is an Appointment whose status is "Available". An approved provider creates slots from one of their own appointment types.

* {{POST /api/slots {appointmentTypeId, startTime}}} creates an Available appointment. The end time is the start time plus the type's duration.
* {{GET /api/slots/mine}} returns the provider's own slots.
* {{DELETE /api/slots/{id}}} soft-deletes a slot, but only if it's still Available.
* Add {{Available}} to the status list the API understands, so open slots stop showing as Scheduled.

Acceptance criteria: the provider must be approved and must own the appointment type; reject a start time in the past; reject overlap with the provider's existing appointments; tests for each.

column30:
h3. User Story

As a user (client or service provider), I want dedicated, responsive registration and login screens so that I can easily sign up and securely access the booking system.

h3. Description

Implement the frontend client-facing UI, forms, and navigation for the authentication flow in BAAAM Scheduling. This ticket covers the visual layouts, client-side input validations, account type switching, dynamic form controls for service providers, and routing transitions.

h3. Acceptance Criteria

h4. Layout & Navigation:

* Full-page authentication layout active on /login, /signup, and /signup/provider (main app navigation/header hidden).

* Direct navigation links between Login and the appropriate Signup screen based on selected account type (selecting Service Provider routes to /signup/provider; selecting User routes to /signup).

h4. Login Flow (/login):

* Role toggle to switch between User and Service Provider.

* Username and password inputs with client-side required field checks.

* Password visibility toggle (eye icon) to show/hide plaintext.

* UI state and alerts for invalid login attempts.

h4. Standard User Registration (/signup):

* Form fields: First Name, Last Name, Username, Email, Phone Number, Password, and Confirm Password.

* Client-side validation: Required fields, valid email format, and password confirmation match.

h4. Service Provider Registration (/signup/provider):

* Includes all standard user registration fields.

* Multi-select service category picker (Medical, Beauty, Fitness) requiring at least one selection.

* Dynamic credential sections that expand based on selected service categories.

* Users can filter notifications by All, Medical, Beauty, and Fitness, with a clear active filter state.
* Users can mark individual notifications as read or mark all notifications as read.
* Changes to read status persist and update any existing unread notification count.
* Notifications associated with an appointment link to the relevant appointment details, where supported.
